stem: Nandini has a $3$ by $3$ magic square whose magic sum is $15$. She multiplies every entry by $4$.

parts.text: Which claim correctly states what happens?

options.text: The grid stays a magic square and the magic sum becomes $15 \times 4 = 60$.
Call the answer a single entry, and stop at that one cell.
The new magic sum $60$ forces each old entry to have been multiplied by $4$, instead of updating the sum from the multiply-by-$4$ change.
Fill or reject the grid by checking only one row of $1$ through $9$, ignoring the multiply-by-$4$ change on every entry.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Multiplying every entry by $4$ keeps the magic-square property and multiplies the magic sum by $4$, so the new sum is $60$.

teacher.key_rationale: Multiplying every cell by $4$ keeps a magic square and scales the magic sum by $4$ to $60$. Naming only one entry, reversing sum and the multiplier, or ignoring the transform all miss that hinge.
